Energy Transition Systems

IBEW outside construction and utility locals

NFPA 70E, NFPA 855 energy storage, NEC Article 690 photovoltaic systems and utility interconnection practice

The plant a utility is building now: solar, storage, charging and the substation that ties them together. Direct current behaves differently, and every station here is about that difference.

The ladder

  • NFPA — NFPA 70E — Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace

What it proves

Competency: Commission and isolate photovoltaic, storage and charging systems

Demonstrated with a mastery run on 3 of its 6 stations, against NFPA 70E Standard for Electrical Safety in the Workplace; NFPA 855 Standard for the Installation of Stationary Energy Storage Systems; NFPA 70 National Electrical Code Article 690 Solar photovoltaic systems.

These stations also count toward:

  • Fall Protection (1 of this track's stations count toward it)
  • Lockout/Tagout and the control of hazardous energy (3 of this track's stations count toward it)

Badges

Each passed level earns an Open Badges 2.0 assertion naming the level, its tasks and their conditions, its lessons and the standards it evidences, with the attempts behind it as evidence, and sends an xAPI statement. Passing level 20, the capstone, climbs the whole track.

A run demonstrates mastery when it earns two or more stars, records zero unsafe actions, answers every interruption it was given, and finishes within 1.5 times the station's par time. One mastery run on enough of a competency's stations earns "demonstrated"; mastery runs on three different days earn "consistent". No other rule earns a competency.

Certification the work leads to: NFPA 70E, NFPA 855 energy storage, NEC Article 690 photovoltaic systems and utility interconnection practice. No level claims apprenticeship hours: no registry entry states an equivalence.

Generated from the programme's station modules: lesson counts are read, not typed. The rules are in tools/briefs/ladder-brief.md and the full table in docs/ladders.md.
